This document outlines 
 the testing procedure P1, which must be performed yearly as indicated by Y1 in 
 the above title block.

The 7UT23 is a high Speed 
 biased differential relay suitable for protecting three winding transformers 
 it is extremely Stable during through external 
 faults and will not operate during inrush 
 currents on energizing. It is manufactured by Siemens.

This procedure details 
 the steps required to completely check the proper operation and calibration of 
 the 7UT23 relay ( figure 1 ).

The first draft initiated 
 by eng. Mahmood Abd Allah Hasan at Suze protection management, tested on 4 July 2005 at Suz 
 Cement Substation by eng. Mahmood Abd Allah Hasan, 
 reviewed by protection manager eng. Shaban Ali, accepted and approved by 
 general manager eng. Saad El-Attar, revised by quality control manager eng. 
 Mohamed Omran, and certified by eng. Ali Atiia Eldeeb: Head sector of Canal 
 Western Network and MPIS Canal Zone Coordinator.

A work permit must be issued, the qualified maintenance 
 staff should carry the suitable safety category.
Safety fence with caution marks surrounding work area is required.
Wear your safety equipment as helmet, shoes, breathing mask, safety glass...etc.

Make sure CT secondary circuits are shorted before isolating the relay current 
 circuits for current injection

sections.text:
Preliminary Steps to 
Prepare 
for Relay Testing

items:
Obtain outage for 
 Transformer Protected by this relay.

Check the two bus 
 disconnect Switches are opened and tagged.

Inspect the CT 
 secondary circuits and all cables supplying the relay including matching CTs .

Use the station 
 drawings to isolate the following:
Breaker trip coils.

Breaker failure 
 scheme associated with the relay.

Disturbance alarms 
 and fault recorder associated with the relay.

Carefully follow these 
 test procedure steps:

This procedure is used 
 to perform off load relay testing.

Look at the REA panel 
 nameplate and check that this EEA system designation agrees with the

Power transformer that 
 has been taken out of service for maintenance

Check there is no AC 
 current form CT's by using a clip on ammeter.

Check there is no AC 
 voltage form VT's by using a voltmeter.

Connect the secondary 
 injection test terminal to phase (R) terminal on UHV side terminal block.

Slowly increase the 
 current until the relay operates, as indicated by the Light Emitting Diode ( 
 LED ) on the relay front panel.

Record the operating 
 (differential) current and check that this is within: ( 10% ) of the 
 expected current as stated in the maintenance file.

Check the relay trip 
 contacts are closed when the relay picks up and that these contacts open as 
 the current is reduced.

Repeat the same for 
 the alarm contact.

Switch off the 
 secondary injection test set.

Press the reset button 
 on the relay front panel and check that the led indicator resets and the alarm 
 contact open.

Repeat the steps from 
 1 to 7 for phases S , T on UHV side.

Repeat the steps from 
 1 to 7 for phases R , S and T on HV side.
Repeat the steps from 1 to 7 for phases R , S and T on LV side.

sections.text:
NOTE: Before 
removing the AC operating (injection) current Check there is no DC on the relay.

items:
Inject current until 
 the relay operates and switch off the test set.

Connect the timed 
 contact of the relay to the" stop timer" terminals of the secondary injection 
 set.

Switch on the current 
 suddenly and note the operate time.

Record the relay 
 operate time, this should be < 30 mSec.

sections.text: Return The Relay and Associated Equipments to Service

items:
Verify the test result 
 match the relay setting, If not consult technical services.

Trip the circuit 
 breaker associated with the relay.

Return relay to service by reconnecting the relay terminals which had been 
 isolated before, and make sure that CTs and VTs secondary circuits are 
 in normal conditions.

Any equipment 
 associated with the relay which had been isolated before must be returned 
 toservice by the following restoration steps.
Breaker trip coils.

Breaker failure scheme 
 associated with this relay.

Disturbance alarm and 
 fault recorder associated with this relay.

sections.text: Request Power Transformer to be Returned in Service

items:
Take 
 crossed readings of all AC currents and voltages from both HV and LV sides and 
 compare them to those for normal load condition.

Check that these 
 readings agree with station meters: MW, MVAR, Ammeters and power factor

Place a copy of the 
 test result in the field maintenance file.
